📝 Although I didn't specifically target TLPI at the university market as I wrote it, by now I've had emails from a number of university teachers who are using TLPI as a required text or as recommended reading for courses on Linux or UNIX system programming. I'm very interested to find out more details about the use of TLPI in university courses, with the idea in mind of improving a future edition of the book for use in that market. item.title: Cannabinoids remove plaque-forming Alzheimer's proteins from brain cells (2016)
item.description:
📝 It has long been known that amyloid beta accumulates within the nerve cells of the aging brain well before the appearance of Alzheimer’s disease symptoms and plaques. They demonstrated that exposing the cells to THC reduced amyloid beta protein levels and eliminated the inflammatory response from the nerve cells caused by the protein, thereby allowing the nerve cells to survive. In separate but related research, his lab found an Alzheimer’s drug candidate called J147 that also removes amyloid beta from nerve cells and reduces the inflammatory response in both nerve cells and the brain.
🔗 Read more: https://www.salk.edu/news-release/cannabinoids-remove-plaque-forming-alzheimers-proteins-from-brain-cells/

item.title: "How I write software with LLMs"
item.description:
📝 I thought that I liked programming, but it turned out that what I like was making things, and programming was just one way to do that. Most of that must be because the models are getting better, but I think that a lot of it is also because I’ve improved my way of working with the models. One thing I’ve noticed is that different people get wildly different results with LLMs, so I suspect there’s some element of how you’re talking to them that affects the results.
🔗 Read more: https://www.stavros.io/posts/how-i-write-software-with-llms/

item.title: AI tools are making me lose interest in CS fundamentals
item.description:

item.title: Excel incorrectly assumes that the year 1900 is a leap year
item.description:
📝 Excel incorrectly assumes that the year 1900 is a leap year Applies to: Microsoft Excel for Mac 2011, Excel for Microsoft 365 for Mac, Microsoft Office Excel 2003, Microsoft Office Excel 2007, Excel 2010, Excel 2013, Excel 2016 Feedback Summarize this article for me Symptoms Microsoft Excel incorrectly assumes that the year 1900 is a leap year. When Microsoft Multiplan and Microsoft Excel were released, they also assumed that 1900 was a leap year. Correcting this behavior would break serial date compatibility between Microsoft Excel and other programs that use dates.
🔗 Read more: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoft-365-apps/excel/wrongly-assumes-1900-is-leap-year
